column1: relationships|present|{0} Relate what you notice to one recent exchange, without guessing the other person's feelings.|{0} Consider a recent exchange you can describe from your own experience.

relationships|crossroads|{0} Treat what you learn as a check on a possible agreement, not a reason to decide for the other person.|{0} Keep your own needs and the other person's freedom to decline in view.
relationships|action|{0} Keep this to one exchange you can freely take part in; you do not need to force a response.|{0} Focus on your part in the exchange rather than a result you cannot control.

work|present|{0} Use what you notice to understand one current responsibility, rather than judging your whole career.|{0} Consider a concrete task or recent handoff rather than your worth as a worker.

work|crossroads|{0} Treat the result as information about a work option; it does not replace checking its scope and commitments.|{0} Apply this to the options actually available, including their demands on your time.

work|action|{0} Keep the attempt within a task you own; check with the responsible person before changing a shared commitment.|{0} Focus on the next task you can influence, not an entire career outcome.

creativity|present|{0} Use the result to understand the current draft or working process before judging the project's potential.|{0} Consider the piece as it exists now rather than an imagined finished version.

creativity|crossroads|{0} Treat what you learn as one check on a creative direction, while keeping an earlier version available.|{0} Apply this to the directions you are considering for this particular project.

creativity|action|{0} Keep this to one part of the draft or practice session so you can inspect the result without committing the whole project.|{0} Focus on what the next attempt could teach you about the work.

growth|present|{0} Notice what this reveals about one ordinary situation, without turning it into a verdict on your character.|{0} Consider one recent experience rather than trying to explain your whole identity.
growth|crossroads|{0} Use what you learn to weigh a personal choice; a single experience need not settle it.|{0} Consider how each option would fit your ordinary needs and available support.

growth|action|{0} Keep the attempt small enough for your present capacity and decide afterward whether it is worth repeating.|{0} Answer at the scale of today, without demanding a complete reinvention.
